summary:
Implemented Console.set_window_title in the repository, but nothing was run: tests, mypy, and Black are unverified, and I checked the changes by reading them only.

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 after ERASE_IN_LINE; added Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the format entry "\x1b]0;{title}\x07" and the Control.title(title) classmethod, which passes the title as one two-item tuple.
- rich/console.py: added set_window_title beside show_cursor. It gates only on is_terminal, calls self.control(Control.title(title)), and returns True or False.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: added one elif branch that calls term.set_title(title) for title controls. The Win32 wrapper is unchanged.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an Added heading above Fixed under Unreleased, with a bullet linking PR 2200.
- Tests: test_set_window_title in tests/test_console.py, test_control_title in tests/test_control.py, and test_control_set_window_title (Windows-only) in tests/test_windows_renderer.py.

Open points:
- Console.control() skips dumb terminals, so set_window_title returns True there but writes nothing. This follows the spec's terminal check and reuses the existing path.
- The Console test asserts exact output only when legacy_windows is false.
- No commit was made.
